newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER SHOWCASE-FACTS AND FIGURES FOR CHELSEA V MAN UTD.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-FACTS AND FIGURES FOR CHELSEA V MAN UTD.

text.p: Facts and figures for Saturday's English premier league match between Chelsea and Manchester United at Stamford Bridge:
Chelsea:
Founded in 1905. They have won the English league title once.
Major honours: League champions: 1955. F.A. Cup winners: 1970. League Cup winners: 1965. European Cup Winners' Cup winners: 1971.
Ground: Stamford Bridge, capacity 31,791 during current ground development, eventual capacity 41,000. Record attendance 82,905 v Arsenal in a league match on October 12, 1935
Player-manager: Ruud Gullit (Netherlands)
Record league appearances: Ron Harris, 655, 1962-80
Record number of league goals: Bobby Tambling, 164, 1958-70
Record victory: 13-0; Jeunesse Hautcharage of Luxembourg, European Cup Winners' Cup, first round, second leg, September 29, 1971
Record defeat: 1-8, Wolverhampton Wanderers, English league first division, September 26, 1953
Nickname: The Blues
Manchester United:
Founded in 1878 as Newton Heath, changed name to Manchester United in 1902. They have won the league title 10 times

Major honours: League champions: 1908, 1911, 1952, 1956, 1957, 1965, 1967, 1993, 1994, 1996. F.A. Cup Winners: 1909, 1948, 1963, 1977, 1983, 1985, 1990, 1994, 1996. League Cup winners: 1992. Double winners: 1994, 1996. European Cup champions: 1968. European Cup Winners' Cup winners: 1991.
Ground: Old Trafford, capacity 55,500.
Manager: Alex Ferguson
Record league appearances: Bobby Charlton, 606, 1956-73
Record number of league goals: Bobby Charlton, 199, 1956-73
Record victory: 10-0, Anderlecht in the preliminary round, second leg of the European Cup, September 26, 1956
Record defeat: 7-0 to Blackburn Rovers, April 10, 1926. 7-0 to Aston Villa, December 27, 1930. 7-0 to Wolverhampton Wanderers, December 26, 1931. All league matches.
Nickname: Red Devils
League meetings between the two sides at Stamford Bridge over the past ten seasons starting in 1985-86:
Fascinating facts:

- Chelsea should have been the first English representatives in the inaugural European Cup following their league title victory in 1955. But the English Football League barred them from playing. Manchester United won the championship the following season and, despite League opposition, took their place in Europe's top tournament.

- United are much happier playing Chelsea in London than in Manchester. They have been beaten at Stamford Bridge just three times in the league in the last 22 years. In the same period Chelsea have lost just twice at Old Trafford.
- British Prime Minister John Major supports Chelsea. So does former Conservative heritage secretary David Mellor, who now hosts a soccer phone-in on national radio.

- Mellor will face competition from the club he supports from Saturday. Chelsea are using their clash against United to launch Radio Chelsea which will broadcast team news and interviews with players every match day.

- The Blues' other famous supporters are the ex-servicemen from the nearby Royal Chelsea Hospital. The club has a tradition of providing them with free match tickets and at each home game a number of them can be spotted in the main stand clad in distinctive full-length scarlet coats.

- Chelsea may never have existed if it had not been for the original owner of Stamford Bridge who turned down advances from the powerful Great Western Railway to buy the site in 1904. He pressed ahead with plans to turn it into a major sports venue. Chelsea Football Club was formed the following year and has been based at the Bridge ever since.

- United completed their first domestic double when they beat Chelsea in the 1994 F.A. Cup final weeks after clinching the league title. They repeated the feat last year to become the first English side to win the "double double".
